title: Regularization — Round Weights or Sparse Weights
key_insight: L2 regularization smoothly shrinks weights and is called ridge for linear regression. L1 can push some weights exactly to zero and is called lasso.
body:
## Round Weights or Sparse Weights

Two landlords charge differently: one charges increasingly for large weights, while the other charges the same amount for each step away from zero.

L2 regularization smoothly shrinks weights and is called ridge for linear regression. L1 can push some weights exactly to zero and is called lasso.

Scale features before comparing penalties. Otherwise a feature’s unit changes how large its weight must be and therefore how much rent it pays.
common_mistakes: Applying penalties before putting features on comparable scales.
Choosing regularization strength on the test set.
Assuming a zero lasso weight proves a feature is useless in every context.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Round Weights or Sparse Weights” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: It reduces brittle fits and stabilizes models with many or overlapping features.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Round Weights or Sparse Weights” story, explain Regularization without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
